claims.statement: PV component degradation and failure can reduce lifetime energy yield, supporting downtime as a measurable loss, but neither spare scarcity nor reservation willingness is quantified for the proposed cohorts.
Installers, O&M firms, owners, and insurers are plausible payers for reduced downtime, but no fleet census, stockout record, price test, or reservation commitment exists.
The founder can own the control point only by purchasing and testing specific inventory after paid fleet demand is evidenced; no reserve or exclusive supply is currently owned.

IEA PVPS documents diverse PV failure modes and the importance of component life to lifetime yield, while EU policy supports a growing long-lived solar stock; this does not establish which inverter models will become scarce.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Service operations lead, asset manager, business owner, or claims manager
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Aggregate demand across small installers, stay multi-brand, disclose test provenance, and reserve only equipment cohorts supported by paid fleet census data
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Installer or O&M provider until a fleet reservation agreement is signed
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Installer and O&M service portfolios, beginning with a regional fleet census

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Fleet census and installer revenue share; target below one annual portfolio contribution
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Annual reservations precede service, but inventory cash can remain tied up for years and requires cohort-level limits
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Unvalidated target 35-55% on reservations and 15-30% on dispatched hardware after failures and write-downs
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Central testing and cataloging with qualified electricians performing diagnosis and installation
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Safe storage, product and professional liability, electrical testing, provenance records, waste handling, contracts, and accounting
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Hypothesis: 300-1200 PLN annual reservation per covered commercial system plus 15-30% gross markup and logistics on a dispatched unit
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Inventory purchase, testing, refurbishment, packaging, shipping, payment fees, warranty returns, and disposal

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: OEMs, distributors, refurbishers, insurers, and large O&M firms can create their own regional spares pools or force full-system replacement
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Paid event is an annual part-availability reservation and, when needed, a tested spare or loaner dispatch; measurable loss is PV downtime, emergency sourcing cost, or premature full-system replacement
commercial_mechanics.payer: Solar installer, O&M provider, commercial PV owner, or insurer
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Installed fleet census shows material exposure to an unsupported or long-lead-time model and the customer needs a response-time commitment
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Annual fleet coverage review, new equipment cohort enrollment, or inventory dispatch and replenishment

contrary_evidence: Rapid electronics change may make adapters or full replacement cheaper and safer than stocking legacy units.
True failures may be too infrequent and model-specific to support paid pooled reservations.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Planned purchase of serial-numbered, provenance-checked units and parts under supplier warranties where available
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Source from another vetted seller, use a certified adapter or current-model system replacement, issue a loaner, or refund the unavailable reservation
critical_control_point.current_owner: Distributors, installers, asset owners, liquidators, refurbishers, and recyclers; the founder owns no evidenced reserve
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Installer or O&M provider until a fleet reservation agreement is signed
critical_control_point.duration: Ownership would persist after completed purchase, subject to safe storage, testing validity, and obsolescence
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: The parents' renewable-installation firm can lawfully help identify common field equipment and test a paid reservation with consenting customers, but provides no current inventory, exclusive supply, or customer ownership.
critical_control_point.launch_controller: The founder can purchase inventory after due diligence, while suppliers and qualified electricians control sourcing and safe installation
critical_control_point.renewal: Replenish inventory when dispatches and fleet forecasts reduce coverage below a defined service level
critical_control_point.subject: Tested inventory of named legacy inverters, control boards, adapters, and loaner units

economics.acquisition_route: Paid installed-fleet census and reservation sold through regional installers and O&M providers
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Replicated regional reserves and proprietary failure forecasting could attract an O&M or distributor buyer; 5m PLN likely requires multi-region portfolio contracts over 4-7 years
economics.founder_time: Up to five hours per day with electricians handling field diagnosis and a logistics partner handling fulfillment
economics.gross_margin_basis: Reservation and dispatch revenue less inventory, testing, storage, write-downs, warranty, shipping, disposal, support, and channel share
economics.payback: Target each inventory cohort to be covered by prepaid reservations within twelve months; not evidenced
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 300-1200 PLN annual reservation per covered commercial system plus hardware and logistics at dispatch
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual fleet reservations, replenishment after dispatch, and additional equipment cohorts

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Fleet census, observed failure rates, repair outcomes, interchangeability maps, and salvage yields improve which scarce parts deserve working capital
fingerprint.customer: Regional solar installers, O&M firms, commercial PV owners, and insurers responsible for aging distributed systems
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Installers and O&M providers enroll installed fleets and identify model, firmware, topology, and criticality
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Inventory-backed SLA for a narrowly selected equipment cohort, with tested swaps, optional buyback, and compatibility evidence
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Installer or asset owner pays an annual availability reservation and a dispatch fee when a tested compatible spare or loaner is shipped
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An unsupported or slow-to-source inverter or control board fails and replacement lead time creates costly downtime or a full-system redesign

founder_fit: Data analysis can turn an installed-base census into disciplined inventory and failure forecasts
The family renewable-installation relationship offers a lawful regional equipment sample and pilot route
Customer operations are SLA-driven and can be delegated rather than founder-personality driven
A narrow reserve can fit the ordinary capital ceiling if inventory is purchased only after paid enrollment
risks: Inventory may become obsolete, counterfeit, unsafe, or legally unsellable
Misdiagnosis can dispatch the wrong expensive part and extend downtime
Working capital can become trapped in slow-moving units
OEM or distributor supply recovery can erase scarcity premiums

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: inventory backed availability sla with reservation and dispatch fees
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: purchased tested serial numbered reserve inventory for selected legacy equipment cohorts
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: authentic used refurbished or compatible equipment with verifiable provenance

structure.control_point: owned and tested reserve inventory for selected legacy inverter families
structure.critical_dependency: reliable supply of authentic used, refurbished, or compatible replacement units and parts

thesis: Future operating state (2034): distributed PV fleets stay productive beyond original electronics support cycles through rapid, compatibility-safe swaps. Missing physical and financial mechanism: a data-selected pool of tested legacy inverters, boards, adapters, and loaner units reserved against site-level service promises rather than accumulated as speculative spare stock.
title: Legacy Inverter Swap Reserve
uncertainties: Regional installed-base distribution, failure frequency, and actual lead times by model
Safe interchangeability, firmware, grid-code, and warranty constraints
Authentic supply and refurbishment yield for selected equipment
Reservation price that covers write-downs while remaining cheaper than customer alternatives
